filing-20260807-5215.point: CEBA says the show cause issues are complex and need region-specific solutions worked out with stakeholders.
filing-20260807-5215.quote: Granting the requested abeyance will promote administrative efficiencies by allowing time for CAISO and stakeholders—including CEBA and its members—to work collaboratively

filing-20260807-5215.point: A 90-day abeyance would not materially slow the reforms and would give the mid-November filings stakeholder feedback.
filing-20260807-5215.quote: a 90-day extension would not materially impede the Commission’s objectives for advancing reforms quickly

filing-20260807-5215.point: CEBA asks for expedited action on the motions.
filing-20260807-5215.quote: CEBA respectfully requests that the Commission grant these motions in an expedited manner.

motion-el26-71-caiso-abeyance.point: CAISO wants 90 days from the response deadline to November 16, 2026, aligned with the Participating Transmission Owners' requests.
motion-el26-71-caiso-abeyance.quote: hold the instant proceeding in abeyance for 90 days from the deadline to respond

motion-el26-71-caiso-abeyance.point: The filing is meant to address all preliminary findings and five reform categories in the order, with simultaneous PTO filings.
motion-el26-71-caiso-abeyance.quote: will address all the preliminary findings and five categories of reforms set forth in the Order to Show Cause, as appropriate for the CAISO region.

motion-el26-71-caiso-abeyance.point: CAISO's Large Load stakeholder initiative is the vehicle; an issue paper came in January 2026 and a technical-requirements straw proposal in June 2026.
motion-el26-71-caiso-abeyance.quote: The CAISO’s ongoing Large Load stakeholder initiative will become the vehicle for CAISO reforms to address the Order to Show Cause.

motion-el26-71-caiso-abeyance.point: Most tariff changes should take effect on approval; software-dependent items such as new settlement charges may take longer.
motion-el26-71-caiso-abeyance.quote: The CAISO expects that the vast majority of its tariff revisions will be able to become effective as soon as approved by the Commission.

motion-el26-71-caiso-abeyance.point: The schedule runs a straw proposal in August, a draft final in September, governing body votes October 20 and 28, and a November 16 FERC filing.
motion-el26-71-caiso-abeyance.quote: two discrete proposals: a straw proposal in August and draft final proposal in September, before seeking Western Energy Market Governing Body and Board of Governors approval

motion-el26-71-caiso-abeyance.point: CAISO and the PTOs keep the existing split of responsibilities and coordinate weekly.
motion-el26-71-caiso-abeyance.quote: including multiple weekly meetings among various teams of subject-matter experts for the categories of issues identified by the Commission.

filing-20260803-5170.point: DCRT owns the 125-mile, 500 kV Ten West Link, about 100 miles of it in Arizona but all inside the CAISO balancing authority area.
filing-20260803-5170.quote: DCRT owns and manages the 125-mile, 500 kilovolt Ten West Link Transmission Line

filing-20260803-5170.point: As a transmission-only company with no load or network customers, DCRT says franchised-utility tariff provisions do not fit it.
filing-20260803-5170.quote: DCRT is not a Load Serving Entity (“LSE”), has no network customers, and every mile of its transmission facility is part of the CAISO controlled grid

filing-20260803-5170.point: A large load withdrawing near the Arizona end would run against the line's prevailing westbound flows.
filing-20260803-5170.quote: a large load withdrawing energy at or near the Arizona portion of the line would run counter to those prevailing flows.

filing-20260803-5170.point: DCRT questions whether the 50 MW large load threshold suits its system.
filing-20260803-5170.quote: it is not clear to DCRT that a 50 MW threshold is appropriate.

filing-20260803-5170.point: DCRT plans a single-location cost data posting and a pro forma cost recovery agreement, and must resolve California and Arizona jurisdiction over construction.
filing-20260803-5170.quote: DCRT must resolve the state-level issue of which entity will have the right to construct assets interconnecting with DCRT’s line

filing-20260803-5170.point: DCRT's filing would track the CAISO proposal, which the CAISO Board takes up October 28, 2026.
filing-20260803-5170.quote: DCRT’s proposed November 16, 2026 filing will address each of the OSC’s directives that implicates DCRT’s TO Tariff, based on the CAISO proposal then before the Commission.

filing-20260803-5170.point: DCRT asks that the briefing question deadline also be tolled for 90 days.
filing-20260803-5170.quote: DCRT requests that the deadline to respond to the briefing questions also be tolled for 90 days.

filing-20260803-5227.point: The motion is conditional on the pending rescission request and is moot if that request is granted.
filing-20260803-5227.quote: if that Motion to Rescind is granted, the Cities’ abeyance request will be moot.

filing-20260803-5227.point: The Six Cities rely on the show cause order's offer of an abeyance of up to 90 days.
filing-20260803-5227.quote: to hold, for up to 90 days, all or certain aspects of this FPA section 206 proceeding in abeyance, including the deadline to respond to this order.

filing-20260803-5227.point: The cities need time to coordinate with CAISO's stakeholder proceeding and with co-owners and contract counterparties.
filing-20260803-5227.quote: the Six Cities will need an additional 90 days to prepare responses to the Show Cause Order, develop potential revisions to each of their TO Tariffs

filing-20260803-5227.point: Any tariff revisions may need approval from a Public Utility Board or City Council.
filing-20260803-5227.quote: each City will need to evaluate whether proposed revisions to their TO Tariffs to address the Show Cause Order require review and approval by the City’s Public Utility Board or the City Council

filing-20260803-5166.point: The Joint PTOs seek a 90-day full abeyance of the 60-day response deadline to prepare section 205 TO Tariff filings.
filing-20260803-5166.quote: The Joint PTOs seek a 90-day full abeyance of the current 60-day deadline to respond to all issues raised in the OSC

filing-20260803-5166.point: Tariff changes will vary by PTO because some serve load and others do not.
filing-20260803-5166.quote: some PTOs serve load while others do not, for example

filing-20260803-5166.point: Filing on August 17 would likely conflict with CAISO's design, so the Joint PTOs want a coordinated set of filings.
filing-20260803-5166.quote: Filing tariff revisions on August 17 would require the Joint PTOs to submit tariff provisions that would likely conflict with the CAISO’s design

filing-20260803-5166.point: The Joint PTOs read the co-location, flexible service and proximate generation findings as aimed at the CAISO Tariff.
filing-20260803-5166.quote: the third, fourth, and fifth issues – co-located load, flexible services, and proximate load – are primarily directed at the CAISO Tariff

filing-20260803-5166.point: CAISO's Board acts October 28, so CAISO Tariff revisions are unlikely to be final until near November 16.
filing-20260803-5166.quote: The CAISO does not currently plan to seek Board approval until October 28, just over two and a half weeks before a 90-day extended filing deadline

filing-20260803-5166.point: The expected filings cover study, application and operational procedures plus transparency, cost recovery, financial security and rate treatment.
filing-20260803-5166.quote: present revisions to the TO Tariffs to include study, application, and operational procedures for the interconnection of large loads

filing-20260803-5166.point: The Joint PTOs also ask that the briefing question deadline be tolled for 90 days.
filing-20260803-5166.quote: The Joint PTOs also request to toll the deadline to respond to the briefing questions for 90 days

filing-20260803-5202.point: WAPA placed only its Path 15 Upgrade Project interests under CAISO operational control, an 83-mile 500-kilovolt line.
filing-20260803-5202.quote: WAPA only placed under the operational control of the CAISO its rights and interests in the Path 15 Upgrade Project, a single, approximately 83-mile, 500-kilovolt transmission line

filing-20260803-5202.point: WAPA keeps the right to use its own tariff for interconnections to the Path 15 Upgrade where CAISO provisions are inconsistent.
filing-20260803-5202.quote: including use of its own Tarif or OATT for interconnections to the Path 15 Upgrade to the extent the CAISO provisions are inconsistent.

filing-20260803-5202.point: WAPA is exempt from FERC jurisdiction under FPA section 201(f) as a federal entity.
filing-20260803-5202.quote: WAPA is a non-public utility that is exempt from the Commission’s jurisdiction pursuant to Section 201(f) of the Federal Power Act.

filing-20260803-5202.point: WAPA will keep coordinating with CAISO and file tariff revisions if it finds changes are needed.
filing-20260803-5202.quote: WAPA will file proposed revisions to its Tariff with the Commission in due course.

filing-20260731-5157.point: Each city runs a municipal system inside CAISO's area and depends on CAISO and SCE to deliver most of its resources.
filing-20260731-5157.quote: the Cities are dependent upon the CAISO and SCE for the delivery of the majority of these resources.

filing-20260731-5157.point: The cities are non-public utilities exempt under FPA section 201(f), the ground the show cause order named for rescission on request.
filing-20260731-5157.quote: Each of the Six Cities is a non-public utility that is exempt from the Commission’s jurisdiction pursuant to Section 201(f) of the Federal Power Act.

filing-20260731-5157.point: The cities promise to coordinate with CAISO on the response and on their TO Tariff load interconnection provisions.
filing-20260731-5157.quote: the Six Cities will coordinate and cooperate with the CAISO in responding to the Show Cause Order, to the extent that the CAISO requests assistance from the Six Cities

filing-20260731-5157.point: CAISO supports the motion, and each city will file its own TO Tariff changes if needed.
filing-20260731-5157.quote: The Six Cities have conferred with the CAISO and are authorized to state that the CAISO supports this motion.

report-el26-71-caiso.point: CAISO says California's planning, led by the CEC, CPUC and CAISO, differs from the capacity-short markets in other regions.
report-el26-71-caiso.quote: California's integrated resource and transmission planning framework is fundamentally different from many other organized markets that are confronting capacity shortfalls

report-el26-71-caiso.point: The CEC forecasts data center load in the CAISO grid of 1.8 GW by 2030 and 4.9 GW by 2040.
report-el26-71-caiso.quote: the CEC forecasts data center load in the CAISO grid to increase by 1.8 gigawatts (GW) by 2030 and 4.9 GW by 2040

report-el26-71-caiso.point: State projections in the 2025-2026 Transmission Plan have load growing 15 GW by 2035 and 20 GW by 2040.
report-el26-71-caiso.quote: California load will grow by 15 GW by 2035 and 20 GW by 2040

report-el26-71-caiso.point: CAISO reports no systemic generation adequacy shortfall comparable to other regions.
report-el26-71-caiso.quote: Current planning assessments do not indicate a systemic generation adequacy shortfall comparable to those in other regions.

report-el26-71-caiso.point: Nearly 36 GW of new generation and storage came online for CAISO load from January 2020 to March 2026, including more than 16 GW of storage.
report-el26-71-caiso.quote: nearly 36 GW of new generation and storage capacity coming online to serve CAISO load between January 2020 and March 2026

report-el26-71-caiso.point: CAISO's 2026 summer assessment finds a surplus of over 2.5 GW against the 1-in-10 reliability standard.
report-el26-71-caiso.quote: The CAISO’s 2026 analysis indicates that the current portfolio meets that target with a surplus of over 2.5 GW.

report-el26-71-caiso.point: Peak load in the WEIM region fell 3.8 percent in 2025 from 135.3 GW to 130.1 GW.
report-el26-71-caiso.quote: Peak market load in the Western Energy Imbalance Market (WEIM) region was 130.1 GW in 2025, down 3.8 percent from the 2024 peak of 135.3 GW.

report-el26-71-caiso.point: The Large Load stakeholder initiative is the vehicle for the show cause response, with a FERC filing on November 16, 2026.
report-el26-71-caiso.quote: The CAISO’s Large Load stakeholder initiative will become the primary vehicle for CAISO reforms to address the Order to Show Cause.
